{{About|the notion used in the context of [[linear complementarity problem]]s|the one used in the context of Markov-chain|Continuous-time Markov chain#Definition}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''Q-matrix''' is a square [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] whose associated [[linear complementarity problem]] LCP(''M'',''q'') has a solution for every vector ''q''.

== Properties ==

* ''M'' is a Q-matrix if there exists ''d'' > 0 such that LCP(''M'',0) and LCP(''M'',''d'') have a unique solution.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Karamardian|first=S.|date=1976|title=An existence theorem for the complementarity problem|journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications|language=en|volume=19|issue=2|pages=227–232|doi=10.1007/BF00934094|s2cid=120505258|issn=0022-3239}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Sivakumar|first1=K. C.|last2=Sushmitha|first2=P.|last3=Wendler|first3=Megan|date=2020-05-17|title=Karamardian Matrices: A Generalization of $Q$-Matrices|class=math.OC|eprint=2005.08171}}</ref>
* Any [[P-matrix]] is a Q-matrix. Conversely, if a matrix is a [[Z-matrix (mathematics)|Z-matrix]] and a Q-matrix, then it is also a P-matrix.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Berman, Abraham.|title=Nonnegative matrices in the mathematical sciences|date=1994|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|others=Plemmons, Robert J.|isbn=0-89871-321-8|location=Philadelphia|oclc=31206205}}</ref>
